A Reading Map for the idle() Journal

Twenty-four entries so far, grouped by the question each one asks. A map of where to start in the idle() journal, depending on what you want to know.

한국어로 읽기 →

Before this one, this journal holds twenty-four entries, written between 22 October and 4 November 2026, and the list on the journal page runs newest first. That order is good for following along, but not for finding your way in. This entry is a map: those twenty-four, grouped by the question each one asks. It adds no new facts about the music; it only points. The music is made with AI (Suno); the lyrics are drafted by AI and reviewed by a person.

If you want to know how the music is made

  • How an AI Lo-Fi Song Gets Made is the shortest way in: who hands what to whom, and where we check.
  • The Six Series of idle() explains the series names and song codes that look like code.
  • From Korean Draft C to the First Single and still compiling — One Night, Two Languages each lay a lyric draft beside the lyrics that were finally sung.
  • 82 Draft Lines, 15 Cues counts what a short clip keeps of a long draft.

If you want to see the album as a whole

dear(you); vol.1 is ten songs, and five entries read all ten at once, each by a different measure:

  • The Ten Steps of Feeling: the album plan, from empathy to peace.
  • How One Lyric Skeleton Repeats Across Ten Songs: the shared structure of the lyric sheets.
  • Ten Titles, Read as Sentences: tense, speaker and tone of the titles.
  • Who Speaks in the Ten Titles?: a count of the pronouns.
  • The Tempo Ladder of Ten Songs: the written BPM, song by song.

If you read only one of these, the first gives the frame the other four count inside.

If you want to start from one song

Entries on single songs, or on a pair, follow the track order:

  • Songs 01 and 10: Check In Before You Fix on the first song, and Open with a Question, Close with Comfort on the first and last as a pair.
  • Song 02: Tell Me, and You Needn't Answer.
  • Songs 03 and 04: Admitting Fear Instead of Fixing It on song 03, then A Developer's Song Without the Word "Developer" on 03 and 04 together.
  • Songs 04 and 07: The Same Sentence in Two Songs.
  • Song 05: Putting Rest at the Center.
  • Song 06: Six Someones, One Spoken Line.
  • Song 08: Two Lists, One Day.
  • Songs 09 and 10: Closing the Album with Its Slowest Song.

If you want to know why every song has two versions

Each song exists in an English-main version and a Korean-main version. English by a Woman, Korean by a Man gives the rule that splits them, and Whispers in the Other Language counts the whispered lines that switch language between the two.

If you want to know what comes next

One Day, Four Albums lays out the four-album plan for Season 1. Only the first album is out, and that entry says which parts of the plan are still open.

And the site itself

One Entry, Twelve Languages explains how an entry becomes up to twelve pages. A related detail from the list itself: twenty-one of the twenty-four entries exist in all twelve languages, and the three newest, the tempo ladder, the pronoun count and the language entry, are published in Korean and English only so far.

What this map does not say

  • It does not rank the entries. Grouping is our reading, not a measure of which entries are read most; we have not measured that.
  • It does not promise an order. Each entry stands alone, and any of them is a fair place to begin.
  • It does not cover what is not written yet.

If you have read one entry and want the next, follow the links inside it; most point to a neighbour.
